correction: An earlier receipt reported 1617 tok/s and $0.046 per million tokens as the CUDA peak. That was an artifact of the sweep stopping at concurrency 16, not a hardware ceiling. The same card sustains 7081 tok/s at concurrency 128 for $0.0106 per million, 4.4x better, with TTFT still 770ms.
tuning_flags_verdict: NOT demonstrated to help. At MATCHED concurrency 16 the tuned run measured 1596 tok/s against the stock run's 1617 -- identical within noise. prefix-caching, chunked-prefill, max-num-seqs 256 and util 0.95 may still matter for shared-prefix or long-prompt traffic, which this uniform-prompt sweep does not exercise. The improvement reported here comes from testing higher concurrency, not from the flags, and attributing it to them would be wrong.
whose_cost: The $0.27/hr is RENTED TEST CAPACITY. In merc's supply model the rig owner pays electricity and merc pays per accepted unit, so this figure is a proxy for supplier margin -- tokens per kilowatt-hour -- not merc's cost.
caveat: Qwen2.5-1.5B fp16 on one A5000, uniform 128-token completions. Not a claim about larger models.
